functions.semantics: eventsArray first (malloc 1028). Each record is published into the reloaded data->events array at a byte cursor (+=4), then child = child->next.

Writes 0x55555556 into +0x48 ([sp,#0x60]) from movw 0x5556 (0x28d2d8) + movt 0x5555 (0x28d2e0). Spills data (r9) into +0x00 ([sp,#0x18]) and the spSkeletonJson pointer (r8) into +0x08 ([sp,#0x20]). No allocation, no Json access, no branch.
quirks: 0x28d304 str r1,[sp,#0x60] is the ONLY write of 0x55555556 in the whole 13044-byte function
0x28d310 str r9,[sp,#0x18] / 0x28d314 str r8,[sp,#0x20] are register spills for later blocks (0x28e774, 0x28ea48/0x28ea50); not data products of this block

functions.name: readSkeletonData_animationKeys
functions.address_range: 0x28d318-0x28d3b0 (B3 lookup half; loop head 0x28d318, back edge 0x28e79c, 39 insns)
functions.semantics: Per animation: eight Json_getItem(animation_node, key) calls in address order with results stored to bones [sp,#0x30] (0x28d328), slots -> r4 (0x28d338), ik [sp,#0x34] (0x28d348), transform [sp,#0x38] (0x28d35c), paths [sp,#0x44] (0x28d370), deform [sp,#0x50] (0x28d384), drawOrder [sp,#0x28] (0x28d398), events [sp,#0x4c] (0x28d3ac). The first four use the cached literals from +0x4c..+0x58; the last four rebuild the literal from the pool each iteration (0x28d354/58 paths->0x357e5c, 0x28d368/6c deform->0x357de4, 0x28d37c/80 drawOrder->0x357e64, 0x28d390/94 events->0x357d94). Ends with 0x28d3a4 ldr r1,[sp,#0x28]; 0x28d3a8 cmp; 0x28d3b0 beq 0x28eb28. The slots node stays in r4 and is returned here because B4 re-reads r4 at 0x28d3e4 and 0x28d4c8.
quirks: loop head is inside this block (0x28d318), the preamble above is loop-invariant
eight stores, eight distinct slots: two land in registers/memory in a non-monotonic address order (drawOrder +0x28 before bones +0x30 in the source, but at a lower address)
the lookup node is [sp,#0x1c], the animation node — NOT the root tree (root is [sp,#0x24])
no NULL guard on the animation node; a NULL node would fault exactly as the original does
no allocation and no error path

functions.name: readSkeletonData_animationLegacyDrawOrder
functions.address_range: 0x28eb28-0x28eb40 (B3b, 24 B / 6 insns, out of line at the function tail)
functions.semantics: Reached only from 0x28d3b0 beq 0x28eb28 when the "drawOrder" lookup returned NULL. Re-runs Json_getItem(animation_node, "draworder") (pool 0x28eb24 / add 0x28eb30 -> 0x357e70, lowercase legacy key), stores the result UNCONDITIONALLY into [sp,#0x28] (0x28eb38), then b 0x28d3b4 (B4). No NULL test follows the store.
quirks: store is unconditional: on a second miss it overwrites the slot with the NULL it already held
Json_getItem compares case-insensitively (0x287414 bl strcasecmp@plt), so "drawOrder" and "draworder" are the same query and this retry can never find a node the first lookup missed
with both spellings present, getItem returns the FIRST matching child in list order — not a priority for the camelCase key
whole block is 6 insns with one bl and one b; nothing else is touched

functions.name: readSkeletonData_animationTimelines
functions.semantics: Sums a timeline count per animation group and calls spAnimation_create(animation_node->name, total), then zeroes the created record's +0x08 and publishes slots->child. Sum shape per instruction: bones = sum of child->unk_0c over bones->child chain (0x28d3d0..0x28d3e0, zero-fast paths 0x28ea80 when bones==NULL and 0x28ea40 when bones->child==NULL); slots = same over slots->child (0x28d3f8..0x28d408, skipped when r4==NULL); ik = ik->unk_0c once (0x28d418, no child loop); transform = transform->unk_0c once (0x28d42c); paths = sum over paths->child (0x28d44c..0x28d45c); deform = double loop over deform->child (skins) then skin->child (slots), summing slot->unk_0c (0x28d478..0x28d4a0); drawOrder and events each +1 when the node is non-NULL (0x28d4b4/0x28d4bc). Then 0x28d4c0 ldr r0,[r2,#0x1c] with r2=[sp,#0x1c] -> the animation member key; 0x28d4c4 bl spAnimation_create; 0x28d4d4 str r3(=0),[r0,#0x8]; if r4 != 0 then [sp,#0x2c] = r4->child (0x28d4dc/0x28d4e4) and the B5 loop is entered when that child is non-NULL.
quirks: 0x28d3bc beq 0x28ea80 and 0x28d3c8 beq 0x28ea40 are out-of-line zero-total paths: 0x28ea80 ldr r3,[sp,#0x30] (bones==NULL -> 0), 0x28ea40 mov r3,r2 (child==NULL -> 0); both b 0x28d3e4
the accumulator starts in r3 (bones+slots+ik) and moves to r1 at 0x28d438 add r1,r3,r2; paths/deform/drawOrder/events add into r1

ik and transform are counted from the NODE's own +0x0c with no child loop, while bones/slots/paths sum per-child +0x0c — an asymmetry taken from the instruction stream, not from a stock spine-c source
0x28d418 ldrne / 0x28d41c ldreq r2,[sp,#0x34]: the NULL branch reloads the (zero) node word itself
create arguments: r0 = Json member key of the animation node (no Json_getString("name")), r1 = the summed count
0x28d4c8/0x28d4d8 beq 0x28d640: slots absent skips the sp+0x2c spill entirely, so a stale frame slot survives
spAnimation_create's own body is a synthetic boundary here; +0x08 is written twice (creator: arg1 at 0x281304, then 0 at 0x28d4d4)

open: 0x55555556 read point: the only writer is 0x28d304 and the only reader is 0x28e128 ldrne r1,[sp,#0x60] in the deform block, which feeds 0x28e134 smull r1,r2,r1,r3 and 0x28e13c subne r3,r2,r3,asr#31 (signed truncating /3). That block is NOT recovered here, so the slot is written/documented only; the tests pin the constant by its /3 arithmetic identity over int32 boundaries, not by executing a consumer. Whether B13/B17 reuse the slot is still open (census §7 item 8).

Frame slots +0x24/+0x28/+0x30/+0x3c/+0x40/+0x44/+0x5c are shared scratch: B5 writes +0x28/+0x30/+0x3c (0x28d510/0x28d518/0x28d51c), the bone reader +0x28/+0x30/+0x3c/+0x40, the color reader +0x44, the deform path +0x24. B1..B4 never write them; a future block must re-derive each write before naming them.

Json_getItem is case-insensitive (0x287414 bl strcasecmp@plt), so the drawOrder/draworder double key is one query and B3b can never find what the first lookup missed; with both spellings present the FIRST child in list order wins. The byte stream is recovered exactly (including the unconditional store), but whether the original author intended a case-sensitive key set cannot be decided from this build. This corrects the census §2.9 wording that the fallback makes the camelCase key 'preferred'.

B3's two halves have different loop scopes: the preamble (0x28d2d4..0x28d314) runs once per animations array while the 8-key lookup runs per animation. The census lists 0x28d318 as an outer-loop head (§5.3) and also puts 0x28d2d4..0x28d3b4 in one block (§6); both are true, and the C keeps the split explicit (frameInit vs keys) rather than hiding the preamble in a loop.

timelineCount grouping is asymmetric per instruction: ik and transform contribute node->unk_0c once (0x28d418/0x28d42c, no child loop) while bones/slots/paths sum each child's +0x0c and deform walks skins×slots. Whether this equals the number of timelines the later blocks actually create for ik/transform needs B7/B12 to confirm; nothing here was 'repaired' to match a stock spine-c layout.

animation+0x08 is written twice: arg1 inside the creator (0x281304) and 0 then by 0x28d4d4. Which later instruction increments it (the fill cursor counterpart of data+0x34 at 0x28e784) is outside this batch — open.

0x28ea80 and 0x28ea40 are out-of-line zero-total paths reached from 0x28d3bc/0x28d3c8. They are modelled as 'total = 0' on the two early-exit branches; their bytes are recorded in the receipt as pins but their addresses belong to the tail region the census assigns to the deform/error blocks.

B4 publishes slots->child into [sp,#0x2c] only when the slots node exists (0x28d4d8 beq skips the store), so a frame reused across animations keeps a stale slotsChild when an animation has no slots node. Reproduced as written; no defensive clear was added.
No error path exists in B1..B4/B3b (no setError, no dispose, no NULL check on either creator's return); a NULL spAnimation_create result would be dereferenced at 0x28d4d4 exactly as in the original.

census_cross_check.malloc: B3/B3b/B4 contain no _malloc and no _free, as §3.1 implies (the segment's seven anchors are at 0x28d1cc, 0x28d268, 0x28d2bc, 0x28e154, 0x28e3e0, 0x28e3f8, 0x28e708)
census_cross_check.magic: §7 item 8 verified byte-exactly: 0x28d2d8 movw 0x5556 + 0x28d2e0 movt 0x5555 -> 0x28d304 str r1,[sp,#0x60]; the single read is 0x28e128 ldrne
census_cross_check.contradiction_1: §2.9 says the two drawOrder keys make the camelCase spelling preferred and that the fallback must be preserved. It IS preserved, but because Json_getItem uses strcasecmp the retry is behaviorally void and child order decides. Not a byte-level contradiction — a semantic consequence the census did not state.
census_cross_check.contradiction_2: §5.3 table lists 0x28d318 as an outer-loop head while §6 assigns the surrounding addresses to B3; the resolution is that B3 contains both a one-shot preamble and the loop head (see open item 4). No address is orphaned: 0x28d2d4..0x28d314 runs once, 0x28d318..0x28d3b0 runs per animation.
census_cross_check.note: No instruction-span disagreement found. The earlier wording imprecision about the animations ARRAY base (written at 0x28d2cc, not only at the 0x28e778 loop tail) still stands from the B1/B2 batch.
